expect: ~7 million metric tons of reserves x ~70% mining efficiency x ~40% directed to batteries = ~2 million metric tons (p1.L42-47, Fig. 1 caption)
question: How does the review get from the known global cobalt reserves to the cobalt usable for batteries, and what amount results?
rendered: The review calculates the cobalt usable for battery industries by applying a conservative mining efficiency of 70% and considering that 40% of the mined cobalt is directed toward battery manufacturing. The known global cobalt reserves are approximately 7 million metric tons, so the total usable battery-specific cobalt from the total reserves is reduced to approximately 2 million metric tons.
